subject: OBG
title: Preeclampsia and Eclampsia: Clinical Recognition and Escalation
preview: High blood pressure after mid-pregnancy plus organ injury can signal preeclampsia even without overt proteinuria.

sections.title: Recognize maternal and fetal risk
points: Severe headache, visual symptoms, breathlessness, severe hypertension, upper abdominal pain and seizures warrant urgent assessment.
Evaluate fetal status, maternal laboratory tests and gestation while stabilizing the mother.

sections.title: Seizure protection and care
points: Use a protocol-approved magnesium sulfate regimen with monitoring for respiratory compromise, reflexes and urinary function.
Severe hypertension management, seizure control and the timing of delivery require specialist obstetric coordination.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Proteinuria is not required when other qualifying organ dysfunction is present.
Do not regard absence of edema as evidence that preeclampsia cannot be severe.

quickRevision: Preeclampsia may involve hypertension with kidney, liver, hematologic, pulmonary or neurologic consequences.
Eclampsia is new-onset seizure associated with the hypertensive pregnancy syndrome after other causes are considered.
Magnesium sulfate is the established anticonvulsant used in eclampsia pathways; obstetric escalation and delivery planning are essential.

quiz.question: What medication is a key seizure-prevention/treatment agent in eclampsia?
options: Low-dose aspirin as acute seizure reversal
quiz.explanation: Use a protocol-approved magnesium sulfate regimen with monitoring for respiratory compromise, reflexes and urinary function.
